chunks: But they turned away. So We let loose on them the inundation of (the dyke of) al-'Arim, replacing their gardens with two other gardens which bore only bitter gourd, and tamarisks and a few sparse lote-trees.

key_terms.جَنَّتَيْنِ: Two gardens, referring to the replacement of their original fertile gardens
key_terms.سَيْلَ الْعَرِمِ: The flood of Arim, a specific inundation or dam-break event

ai.seo_question: What was the specific punishment sent to the people of Saba for turning away from God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the divine retribution upon the people of Saba for their ingratitude, specifically noting the 'flood of Arim' (often identified as the Great Flood or a specific dam breach) as the mechanism of their downfall. The transformation of their lush gardens into those bearing bitter fruit and thorns serves as a tangible sign of how blessings are withdrawn due to spiritual neglect, a theme frequently cited by scholars like Al-Tabarsi to illustrate the direct correlation between moral conduct and material prosperity.
